trust_decision.summary: Which JSON keys and values an admin may write into the Python source conf/config_module.py (later re-imported) is decided only in update_config; at the pinned commit any key name is accepted and written raw, and any value goes through repr into a re.sub replacement template.

landing_point.why: The summary names 'alert settings configuration'; the /alerts/config handler is the only code that writes conf/config_module.py and reloads it.

fix_sites.entry_point: module-level imports/constants for the same handler (fix.diff:10-48 adds ALLOWED_CONFIG_KEYS and _config_value_to_python)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Only one writer of conf/config_module.py exists; the other source-writing settings route (app/tools/tools.py:777-861, writes conf/config.py) already has an allowlist, so there is nothing to argue away.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The Alerts page must still save the nine webhook/IMAP keys with their types (booleans, IMAP_PORT as int, URL/secret/password as arbitrary strings that may contain quotes or backslashes); a fix that rejects special characters in strings or coerces bool/int wrongly breaks it.

O6_input_shapes: key not in allowlist (arbitrary key name appended raw as source text)
key containing regex metacharacters (key interpolated unescaped into pattern)
value of wrong type for key (bool for int, int for bool, list/dict/null)

O7_producer.where: app/alerts/alerts.py:88 (importlib.reload of conf.config_module, imported across app e.g. app/modules/notify_user/webhook.py:8)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An editable OLLAMA_URL/OLLAMA_MODEL/OLLAMA_KEY save route that writes conf/config_module.py with the old loose key/value handling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The page states OLLAMA_* in config_module.py are read-only here; making them editable alongside the existing config.py editor is a natural feature request.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A list/str formatter in the conf/config.py writer that builds the replacement via re.sub template or skips repr for the 'list' type.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same function already special-cases a 'list' type by splitting a string; a maintainer could hand-format it instead of using repr.

O9_family: code injection via unvalidated keys/values written into a Python config module that is re-imported (CWE-94/CWE-20)

O10_build.project_tests: tests/ with tests/conftest.py; tests/alerts/test_alert_ingest.py covers alert ingestion, not /alerts/config; the fix adds no tests.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a key allowlist and keep the re.sub(pattern, f'{key} = {repr(val)}') write, leaving string values to be reinterpreted as a regex replacement template.

out_of_scope_notes: app/tools/tools.py:777-861 writes conf/config.py source from admin input; already allowlisted with a callable replacement (tools.py:841-842), different file and sink.
unverified: Not run: the published fix still passes repr(str) output as a re.sub replacement string (fix.diff:80-83), so backslash escapes in a stored string may be collapsed and could break out of the literal; this is a possible HOW-type residual worth confirming before using the published fix as the reference.
